acceptance_criteria.criterion: PHPStan reports no new errors in EpisodeListPage.php
All manual testing scenarios pass (0, <20, 20, >20, 100+ episodes)
Pagination URLs preserve application routing parameters
Form submissions with pagination work correctly end-to-end

summary: Static analysis verification: PHPStan reports zero errors in EpisodeListPage.php (--configuration phpstan.neon, --memory-limit=900M).
Test suite verification: all 60 tests pass with no regressions (1 pre-existing skip, 1 pre-existing deprecation warning).

URL structure analysis confirmed correct: ArrayPagination.getPageURL() builds pagination URLs from REQUEST_URI query string, preserving all existing parameters (page=EpisodeList, comicID=...) while adding/updating ep_page=N.

Pagination visibility logic confirmed correct: Bootstrap5Renderer.renderPaginationRow() returns '' when getTotalPages() <= 1, covering 0 episodes (getTotalPages=0), <20 episodes (getTotalPages=1), and exactly 20 episodes (getTotalPages=1). Controls only render for >20 episodes.

Form submission with pagination confirmed correct: hidden ep_page field captures getCurrentPage(), and handleRefreshDetails() passes ep_page to getURLEpisodeList($params) which always re-adds page=EpisodeList and comicID=... to the redirect URL.
Error redirect preservation confirmed: failed refresh on page N redirects back to same page N via getURLEpisodeList(['ep_page'=>N]).

comments.note: EpisodeListPage.php handleRefreshDetails(): when ep_page is present but equals '0' (e.g. a crafted request), (int)'0' = 0 is added to the redirect params as ep_page=0. ArrayPagination clamps this to page 1, so there is no functional bug, but the redirect URL carries a semantically incorrect page number. A guard like `if ($epPage !== null && (int)$epPage >= 1)` would keep the URL clean.

EpisodeListPage.php _render(): the hidden ep_page form field always sends the current page on submission (including page 1), so successful-action redirects on page 1 append a redundant ep_page=1 to the URL. Omitting the hidden field when getCurrentPage()==1, or stripping page-1 in getURLEpisodeList, would produce cleaner URLs. Currently harmless.

summary: PHPStan: 0 errors on EpisodeListPage.php (--configuration phpstan.neon --memory-limit=900M).
PHPUnit: 60/60 tests pass, 0 failures, 0 errors (1 pre-existing skip, 1 pre-existing deprecation warning).
AC1 — PHPStan clean: confirmed.

AC2 — Pagination visibility logic verified by code path analysis: GridPagination.getTotalPages() returns 0 for 0 items (0<=1 → hidden), 1 for 1-20 items (1<=1 → hidden), and >=2 for >20 items (>1 → shown). ArrayPagination clamps currentPage to valid range for all episode counts including 100+.

AC3 — URL preservation confirmed: ArrayPagination.getPageURL() reads REQUEST_URI query string, uses parse_str to decode all existing params (including page=EpisodeList and comicID=), sets/updates only the ep_page key, then rebuilds with http_build_query. Routing params cannot be stripped.

AC4 — Form submission round-trip confirmed: hidden ep_page field captures getCurrentPage(); handleRefreshDetails reads ep_page, casts to int, adds to $params; Comic::getURLEpisodeList() always overwrites params with page=EpisodeList and comicID=, so routing params are guaranteed in success and error redirects.
Edge case (non-numeric ep_page): PHP casts both in GET reading and in (int)$epPage, resulting in 0, which ArrayPagination clamps to page 1. No errors.
Edge case (out-of-range ep_page like 9999): ArrayPagination clamps to totalPages. No errors.

comments.note: Submitting the form with no episodes selected (no checkboxes ticked) while grid-action=refresh-details results in handleRefreshDetails() returning early with no user feedback — the page silently re-renders. This is pre-existing behavior unrelated to the pagination change, but could confuse users. Recommend adding a 'No episodes selected' error redirect.

Pre-existing from implementation pipeline: handleRefreshDetails() adds ep_page=0 to the redirect URL when ep_page param is '0'. ArrayPagination clamps this to page 1, so no functional bug, but the URL carries a semantically incorrect page number. A guard `if((int)$epPage >= 1)` would keep URLs clean.

Pre-existing from implementation pipeline: ep_page hidden field always emits current page including page 1, so successful-action redirects on page 1 append a redundant ep_page=1 to the URL. Currently harmless.

summary: WP-003 code review PASS. No blocking issues. EpisodeListPage.php reviewed line-by-line against all four dimensions.
Maintainability: clean, readable code; unambiguous variable names ($allEpisodes, $pagination, $epPage, $params); no unnecessary complexity.

Best practices: ArrayPagination wired correctly via setProvider(); getSlicedItems() correctly replaces full getAll() in loop; ep_page parameter name chosen deliberately to avoid page= routing conflict — good defensive design. getURLEpisodeList() unconditionally reasserts page= and comicID= params, so routing correctness is enforced at the method boundary regardless of what callers pass.

Security: (int)$epPage cast in handleRefreshDetails() prevents injection; out-of-range/non-numeric values safely clamped to page 1 by ArrayPagination. episodes[] already guarded by is_array() check before processing.

Future context: implementation is scoped correctly — pagination state lives exclusively in the rendering layer with no leakage into the fetcher or storage layer. ep_page hidden field pattern is the right solution for POST round-trips.

Three previously identified non-blocking items remain as suggestions: (1) ep_page=0 guard in handleRefreshDetails, (2) omit ep_page hidden field or guard for page 1, (3) follow-up WP for silent no-op UX on empty selection.

comments.note: handleRefreshDetails(): guard ep_page=0 case by changing `if($epPage !== null)` to `if($epPage !== null && (int)$epPage >= 1)`. Currently ep_page=0 is forwarded to getURLEpisodeList, producing a URL with ep_page=0 that ArrayPagination silently clamps to page 1. No functional bug, but the redirect URL carries a semantically incorrect value.

_render(): the ep_page hidden field unconditionally emits getCurrentPage() including for page 1. Successful-action redirects from page 1 carry a redundant ep_page=1. Consider omitting the field when getCurrentPage()==1, or stripping ep_page from getURLEpisodeList params when its value is 1. Currently harmless.

Pre-existing UX gap (out of scope for this WP): handleRefreshDetails() returns early with no feedback when no checkboxes are ticked. The page silently re-renders. Recommend a follow-up WP to add a 'No episodes selected' error redirect at the top of handleRefreshDetails(), matching the error redirect pattern already used below.
No issues found — implementation is clean and correct across all review dimensions.
